items.detail: The codex-tui crate implements an interactive Ratatui client that receives keyboard, paste, resize and focus events, renders application state, and can connect to either an in-process or remote app server. It is a terminal client, not evidence for the separate desktop or IDE products. | README points to the external letta-code package for an interactive terminal UI.
items.note: Interactive terminal chat with streaming and model/thinking commands.

items.detail: The exec crate runs Codex without the full-screen TUI, emitting only the final answer on stdout by default or a JSONL event stream with --json while routing other output to stderr; it also supports starting, resuming and forking threads through the app-server protocol.
items.note: non-interactive exec mode not implemented.

firstPass.note: One-shot headless execution is not implemented.

items.detail: The exec_command tool accepts a command, working directory, optional shell/login behavior, PTY selection, output wait and token limits, and may return a session identifier for continued interaction. Actual execution remains subject to sandbox and approval policy. | The core `bash` tool executes model-supplied commands through the configured sandbox and returns stdout, stderr and exit status; without Quicksand, the sandbox abstraction may be host-backed.
items.note: Shell command execution through shell.ts with timeout, output limits, and optional sandbox via shell.execute tool.

items.detail: Codex parses apply_patch input into explicit add, delete and update operations, resolves paths against a working directory, computes resulting content, and exposes the proposed change map before application. Approval and sandbox policy can still gate the write.
items.note: Workspace file patching is not a specific tool; Branch uses edit (replace) and write primitives instead.

items.detail: The file-search service performs incremental fuzzy path matching over one or more search directories, reports ranked snapshots, supports exclusions and cancellation, and can honor repository-scoped .gitignore rules. It is a path navigator, not a general full-text code-search engine.
items.note: Workspace file discovery exists (files.list) but no dedicated fuzzy path search or .gitignore-aware ranking.

firstPass.note: Workspace file discovery exists (files.list) but no dedicated fuzzy path search or .gitignore-aware ranking.

items.detail: The protocol defines a command-execution approval flow that distinguishes new commands from input sent to an existing terminal and carries command-specific context for the user decision.
items.note: Shell commands require permission and context validation.

items.detail: The protocol defines a separate apply_patch approval flow carrying the proposed file changes, an optional reason, and an optional session-scoped writable root.
items.note: File writes validated and history tracked.

items.detail: Codex models danger-full-access, read-only, workspace-write and external-sandbox execution policies, with network access and writable-root controls where applicable. These policies describe requested authority; enforcement depends on the selected OS or external sandbox backend.
items.note: Workspace confinement enforced; no external sandbox selection.

firstPass.note: Workspace confinement enforced; no external sandbox selection.

items.detail: Codex selects platform-specific sandbox mechanisms: macOS Seatbelt, Linux seccomp-based sandboxing, Windows restricted-token sandboxing, and Windows MXC, with an explicit unsandboxed variant. Backend availability and guarantees differ by host platform.
items.note: Windows desktop app; sandboxing is OS-level.

items.detail: Codex contributes configured and plugin-selected MCP servers into its extension registry and manages MCP event streams; hosted-app MCP contribution is feature-gated. Individual server transports, tools, resources and OAuth behavior depend on server configuration and are not all proven by the prior c | IntentKit connects to remote MCP servers over SSE or streamable HTTP, creates initialized ClientSession instances, discovers tool schemas, and wraps remote MCP tools as native IntentKit/LangChain tools. Only configured registry servers and credentials are usable.

firstPass.note: MCP client connects to configured servers over stdio/HTTP; no plugin registry system exists.

items.note: Skills are stored as SKILL.md files, scanned, versioned, and injected into runtime instructions.

items.detail: The memories subsystem writes retained stage-one outputs into raw_memories.md and per-thread rollout summaries, and recognizes MEMORY.md, memory_summary.md, raw memories, rollout summaries and memory skills when they are read or searched. This is distinct from ordinary thread transcript persistence
items.note: Memory persistence available.

items.detail: Codex records thread rollout items on disk, exposes thread/resume through the app-server protocol, and lets SDK clients reconstruct a thread from its identifier after the in-memory handle is lost. This is transcript/session persistence, separate from the cross-thread memories subsystem. | Rollout storage preserves sessions for continuation.
items.note: Sessions persisted in SQLite.

items.detail: Codex can replace older conversation history with a compacted representation, using distinct pre-turn/manual policies for whether initial context is reinjected and enforcing a maximum compact-user-message size. Compaction is lossy context management, not archival persistence. | When history crosses a threshold, OmniAgent can replace older history with an LLM-generated structured handoff while retaining reviewed-file and transcript references.
items.note: Implemented.

firstPass.note: Context management partial.

items.detail: The multi-agent tool handler parses agent identifiers and exposes tools for spawning and managing subordinate agent threads. Delegation operates through explicit tool calls and thread metadata rather than an implicit autonomous swarm. | Delegates matched tasks to specialized subagents with separate prompts, tools, and context loops; subagents report findings to the main agent. items.note: Branch delegates work to specialists with separate prompts, tools, and result schemas; configured via knowledge.ts.

items.detail: The plugin/app-server protocol defines scheduled-task summaries and hourly, daily and weekday schedule variants. items.note: Feature specific to OpenAI Codex CLI; Branch is personal assistant.
